subject: Customer request: cancelable streaming + abort reason visibility

From: Samir Kapoor <samir@hyperscribe.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: real-time transcript stops on user cancel — any options?

Hey Rishi,

Following up from our support call yesterday — when a user hits ‘stop recording’ we currently see the streaming response terminate and the UI shows "interrupted". In a few sessions (attached session_dump_789.txt + call logs) the model had produced ~70% of the transcript, but when the stream was cancelled we only get an empty 499 response / no partial tokens.

Customer ask: is there a supported way to: 1) gracefully abort streaming and still receive the tokens produced so far, and 2) get a machine-readable abort reason (client_cancel / preempt / oom) so we can surface correct UX states? They prefer a simple SDK hook: onAbort(reason, lastChunk).

We need an answer for the EOW (customer execs are watching). Any workarounds in the meantime?

Thanks,
Samir
Support Lead — HyperScribe

Subject: Fwd: real-time transcript stops on user cancel — field ask (HyperScribe)

Forwarding Samir's note + logs. TL;DR: HyperScribe (prospect in late-stage POC) wants an SDK-friendly "onAbort" hook that returns a reason code and the last emitted tokens when a stream is cancelled, plus server-level visibility so we can tell whether abort was user-initiated or runtime-triggered. They will not accept "we dropped tokens" as a long-term answer.

Immediate asks from my side:
- Is there a realistic short-term mitigation (config, fallback model, header) we can recommend?
- Rough estimate to expose a stable abort reason in the runtime + API header, and to add a minimal SDK callback that surfaces it to customers.
- Are there safety/perf implications if we retain KV cache or partial state on client disconnect?

Background notes included in attachments (call logs + session dump). I can loop HyperScribe into a triage call if that helps. They have a renewal decision in ~3 weeks.

Thanks — Rishi
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: real-time transcript stops on user cancel — field ask (HyperScribe)

Thanks for the context + logs. Quick technical read: the runtime currently treats client disconnects as an early termination (we tear down the execution and return a 499/connection-closed). We do not persist a "partial finalization" artifact by default — streaming tokens are pushed and when the socket closes the stream ends.

Options and constraints:
1) Short-term mitigation (recommended): add a small client-side retry pattern + short-lived fallback to a smaller 7B model for finalization. That can be documented as a "best-effort finish" but it won't solve determinism for user-cancel cases.

2) Runtime/API change (medium effort): expose an "Abort-Reason" response header with enumerated values (client_cancel, preempt, oom, internal_error) plus a final JSON payload with the last buffered tokens when the runtime captures a graceful shutdown. Requires: API semantics update, runtime change to flush buffer on cancel, and SDK change to surface the header/payload. Risk: small perf hit when we buffer longer; need to ensure this does not yield more memory pressure on high-concurrency hosts.

3) SDK change only (low effort): SDK can treat normal socket close as a cancel and surface whatever tokens were received so far (if any). This is a stopgap — it relies on the socket having already received tokens before close.

Estimate: option 2 is ~2 weeks for a small team (runtime + api + tests) + 1 day to add SDK callback stubs; option 3 is ~2-3 days to add the callback and docs. We should consider gating option 2 behind product sign-off and a small rollout (dedicated customers first).

I'll draft a short design doc for option 2 if you want to proceed. Also: need product to confirm compatibility requirements (protocol version, deprecation schedule).

- Dev
Principal Runtime Engineer
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: real-time transcript stops on user cancel — field ask (HyperScribe)

Appreciate the analysis. Product perspective / constraints:
- We can accept option 2 (Abort-Reason header + final payload) but only if the behavior is strictly opt-in for hosted customers and defaulted-on for Dedicated (where customers expect more deterministic behavior). We need to avoid imposing memory/latency regressions on free-tier users.
- Rollout plan: design doc -> API preview (beta header) -> SDK preview -> opt-in by customer -> GA with deprecation of current 499-only behavior.
- Compliance note: for Private deployments we must ensure this does not create persistent partial artifacts in customer's storage unless they explicitly request it.

Please include: perf budget numbers (extra ms and extra memory per connection) and a short compatibility note for SDKs (JS + Python). If we can get a prototype in our staging cluster, we can route HyperScribe traffic there to validate.

Karthik
